business_problem: Lockheed Martin needed a secure, on-premises way to centralize fragmented compute, MLOps tooling, and generative AI best practices so thousands of developers could build with sensitive data without weeks-long environment setup or escalating public-cloud token costs.
solution_summary: Lockheed Martin built an internal AI factory on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD so training, fine-tuning, RAG, and inference could run in a governed environment instead of scattered laptops, ad hoc GPUs, and token-priced cloud APIs. The company created a customized MLOps platform on top of DGX SuperPOD and uses NVIDIA AI Enterprise as the software base, with NVIDIA NeMo Framework and NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supporting model customization and serving. The platform hosts internal chatbots, coding assistants, proposal-analysis tools, and broader AI workloads across text, image, video, signal, and geospatial data. Because the stack runs on premises, developers can access sensitive data and spin up GPU-backed environments in minutes while still using burst cloud capacity only for temporary non-classified needs. That gives Lockheed a reusable secure platform rather than one-off AI projects.

data_flow: Sensitive enterprise data stays inside Lockheed Martin's on-premises AI factory, where teams train, fine-tune, and serve models on DGX SuperPOD. NeMo-based customization and Triton serving connect those models to internal RAG, chatbot, coding-assistant, and proposal-analysis workflows, while the MLOps platform standardizes deployment across many programs.

business_outcome: Lockheed Martin reduced secure environment setup from weeks to minutes, cut training jobs from weeks to days, processes more than one billion tokens per week, supports 7,000 engineers and developers, and consolidated 30-plus models on its internal platform while avoiding the escalating cost of token-based public-cloud APIs.
